identity.title: Unilateral leg swelling: calf circumference difference >3 cm (10 cm below tibial tuberosity), with calf tenderness

technique.how: With the patient supine and legs relaxed, mark a point 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity on each leg and measure calf circumference with a tape at the same level bilaterally. A difference >3 cm (symptomatic side larger) is positive; also note localized tenderness along the deep venous system and pitting edema confined to the symptomatic leg.
technique.prerequisites: Both legs accessible and comparable (no prior amputation, cast, or chronic unilateral disease that already explains asymmetry).
technique.contraindications: None; avoid firm calf compression if DVT is strongly suspected and pain is severe.

interpretation.positive_finding: Calf-diameter difference roughly doubles the odds of DVT (pooled LR+ 1.8); it is the only physical sign with useful rule-in value but is far weaker than the overall Wells score (high probability LR 5.2).
interpretation.negative_finding: No calf-diameter difference (LR- 0.57) or no calf swelling (LR- 0.67) lowers the probability of DVT only modestly; it cannot exclude DVT on its own.
interpretation.pitfalls: Chronic venous insufficiency, lymphedema, cellulitis, Baker cyst, and prior DVT produce asymmetry without acute thrombosis; measuring at different levels or in a dependent leg creates spurious differences. Calf tenderness alone has LR near 1.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: adds 1 Wells point and pushes toward compression ultrasound; negative does not stop work-up if other Wells items or D-dimer are positive.

sources.citation: Goodacre S, Sutton AJ, Sampson FC. Meta-analysis: the value of clinical assessment in the diagnosis of deep venous thrombosis. Ann Intern Med. 2005;143(2):129-139.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on a negative calf measurement to withhold imaging in a patient with moderate/high Wells probability or with symptoms suggesting PE.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Massive swelling with cyanosis or pallor and pain (phlegmasia) or a cold pulseless limb requires immediate vascular imaging and consultation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Pooled estimates had substantial heterogeneity across cohorts; the 1998 RCE reports clinical examination sensitivity ranging 60-96% and specificity 20-72% across studies, reflecting poor reproducibility of unaided exam.

extraction_notes: Numbers are from the Goodacre 2005 abstract (Ann Intern Med, no PMC full text); 95% CIs for item LRs are not in the abstract and are null. The abstract reports 'difference in calf diameter' without stating the 3 cm threshold; the >3 cm cut-off comes from the Wells score definition used by the included studies (verifier: confirm in Goodacre Table 2). Anand 1998 RCE abstract reports only ranges (sensitivity 60-96%, specificity 20-72%) for the overall clinical examination, so no estimate is entered from it. Wells 2006 RCE is cited as the index for score-level stratification (DVT prevalence 5%/17%/53% low/moderate/high).
